---
title: "Engine changelog"
---

This article records changes to the browser engine in `inst/www/` (`mascot.js`, `mascot-motion.js`,
`mascot-host.js`, `mascot-parts.js`, `mascot-geometry.js`, `mascot-faces.js`, `mascot-player.js` and `mascot.css`),
newest first. User-facing R functions and arguments are
covered in `NEWS.md`.

# mascot 0.1.0

**mascot-engine 0.1.0; character-format-version 1.** The engine is versioned with the package; this is the engine of
the first CRAN release.

## Summary

* **One drawing path.** Every character, built-in or your own, is drawn from a character file in format version 1:
  parts and geometry, faces, mood channels, motion tracks, detail bands for small sizes and kit effects. A part item
  can glow in a palette colour, and outlines are painted under the fill so that only their outer half shows. The
  older drawing code and the bridge that drew Tessa through it are gone (#300, #308, #313, #325, #463).
* **Detail bands.** The band comes from the canvas width: micro below 48 pixels, small from 48 to 127 and full from
  128. A band over its limits is refused before anything is painted; the old band stays and the refusal is reported
  once in the browser console (#303).
* **Deterministic.** A frame is worked out from the character and its state only: the engine never reads the clock
  to draw and never calls `Math.random()`.
* **The browser checks what R checks.** It counts drawing work with the same rules and limits as R for each detail
  band, refuses reserved capabilities and requires a `wave` and a `nod` that move, so a character R accepts draws in
  the browser and the other way round. Accessory part ids cannot collide, and the optional parts of the format
  (`requires`, `$schema`, `note` and `x_` keys) are accepted as in R (#304, #306, #312, #328, #493).
* **The host.** It mounts mascots in Shiny apps, saved pages and Quarto or R Markdown pages, keeps updates that
  arrive before a mascot appears, survives re-rendering, works in nested modules, shows connection loss and starts
  again when a page reconnects into a new Shiny session. Shiny keeps one complete state per mount, so a used gesture
  or a dismissed bubble stays that way when an element is replaced (#70, #133, #305, #426).
* **Panels and clicks.** The speech bubble, the menu and the action tooltip share one panel look; the mascot looks
  towards an open bubble or menu. A click does nothing, runs one action or opens a menu; only the action sends
  `input$<id>_click`. Menus open on the side with room, one at a time, and can be disabled; the space kept for the
  bubble lets clicks through (#225, #233, #241, #257, #349, #350, #506).
* **Placement.** Floating corners, inline placement, minimising with a sharp redraw on restore (reported to Shiny as
  `input$<id>_minimised`), a default size capped at 96 pixels on narrow screens with `small_screen = "auto"`, and
  dragging that snaps to the nearest corner or (experimental) stays where it is dropped (#133, #220, #259, #275,
  #513).
* **Motion.** Gestures play from tracks with five easing curves, interruption, reduced motion and a five-second
  deadline. A swap to another character fades the old one out and the new one in, and is instant with reduced
  motion. Idle, mood change, gestures, swaps, minimising, restoring and panel messages each have their own switch
  (#239, #299, #307).
* **Character files stay as they are.** The tests keep frozen copies of the 0.1.0 character files and face kits (the
  shared face drawings that characters name) with their checksums. A test fails when a frozen file changes or goes,
  every frozen character must keep loading, and a shipped face kit can change only on purpose, through a copy for the
  next version and a NEWS line (#467, #554).
* **Light on the page.** Layout reads are batched, mascots scrolled off-screen stop drawing, and a page carries each
  built-in character's data once (#295, #497).
* **Palettes.** R resolves a named palette; the host applies palette colours first, then role overrides, then CSS.
  A swap keeps the palette when the incoming character's own colours carry its id (#336, #358).
* **Styling and version.** Public classes, `--mascot-*` custom properties and the `.mascot-bubble-region` class are
  documented in `?mascot_styling`; everything else is private. `window.mascot.version` gives the version on the
  page, and a page that loads a second copy of the engine in another version keeps the first and says so in the
  browser console (#260, #464, #558).

## Development entries

<details class="engine-dev-entries">
<summary>What changed while 0.1.0 was developed, by topic</summary>

The visual tool some of these changes mention (`tools/visual/`) is no longer in the repository.

<h3 id="dev-drawing">Drawing and the character format</h3>

* **Parts and geometry (`mascot-parts.js`, `mascot-geometry.js`).** `mascot.parts` works out hierarchical 2D
  transforms per frame: reserved ids `root`, `face` and `effects`, unique `snake_case` ids, one accessory per slot,
  acyclic part and anchor order, `keep_upright` and `no_flip`, channel-driven variant switches (`part.switch`), band
  hiding, layer sorting. Lookups of data-named keys go through `own()` (`Object.hasOwn`), so a key cannot reach
  `Object.prototype`. `mascot.geometry` compiles `path`, `circle`, `arc`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `round_rect`,
  `polyline`, `polygon`, `hexagon` and `ref` shapes into cached `Path2D` objects, with linear and radial gradients (2
  to 6 stops), two outlines (`outline`, `outline.second`, per-band overrides), detail strokes and cross-part clipping
  (`style.clip`, guarded against singular matrices). Each draw returns work counters for the budget checks.
* **Player (`mascot-player.js`).** `mascot.runtime` compiles a character once (`compile()`, a weak cache that keeps
  failures) and plays it. `mount()` returns the controller the host uses (`update`, `gesture`, `setMood`, `seek`,
  `redraw`, `setBand`, `pause`, `play`, `holdVisibility`, `destroy`, `current`, `onChange`). A frame is
  `tracks.frameAt()`, then the mood's channels (the reduced ones under reduced motion), then held look, then
  `parts.frame()`, the ground shadow, the part layers, the face and each kit effect in the layer order the data
  declares. Colours are the character's roles, the user's overrides, then the mood's recolour; an explicit user
  colour wins. A patch is validated whole before any state or pixel changes, and a frame is resolved and checked
  before the canvas is cleared (#307).
* **Mood channels, recolour and switches (#302).** Channel names are checked against the rig (`root.*`, `face.*`,
  `effects.*`, part transforms). Values merge in the order part resting defaults, named pose, mood channels, reduced
  channels. `idle`, `thinking`, `happy`, `worried` and `celebrating` are required, and fallback chains end at them
  (`swapMood()`). `recolour` and `reduced.recolour` redirect colour roles before paints and gradients; a cycle fails
  with `invalid_colour`. Item overrides set `fill`, `stroke` and `alpha`; a `switch: { channel, above, variant }`
  applies strictly above its threshold, and anchors follow a changed variant.
* **Face kits and kit effects.** `mascot-faces.js` paints generic face kits; an omitted glow `alpha` is 1. The sweat
  drop and sparkle star use `mascot.parts.sweatProgress()` and `mascot.parts.sparklePulse()`, so the tests of those
  two functions test the drawing's maths. `mascot.faces.effects()` checks the effect value first (code `input_type`
  at `$.effects.<id>`) (#465).
* **Glow (#300).** One item of a part can glow in a palette colour. `glowPass()` draws one blurred pass per fill or
  stroke on a scratch surface sized to that pass, so output never depends on an earlier pass; `backingBlur()` turns
  design units into backing pixels (`blur * cssWidth / 300 * dpr`). Glow is off in the micro band and at alpha 0.
  A fill-and-stroke emitter counts two blurred passes.
* **Outlines (#325).** An item with `outline: true` is painted second outline, outline, fill, then its own `stroke`,
  so only the outer half of an outline shows, as in the drawings. Sela, Neer (outline 3 to 4.5, second 5 to 6.5) and
  Knurl (2.5 to 3.75, 5 to 6.25) have wider outlines to keep the visible weight; the micro outline of Knurl is unchanged.
* **Detail bands (#303).** `bandFor(width)` classifies the untransformed CSS width: micro below 48, small from 48 to
  127.999, full from 128. The host mounts at the band the canvas measures and calls `setBand()` only when the band
  changes. A band over its limits is refused before anything paints: the old band, pixels and state stay, and the
  refusal is reported once per band through `console.warn`. A canvas with no layout width mounts at `full`. The
  canvas is redrawn once after a resize.
* **Tessa (#307, #308, #313).** A format-v1 character mounts in the host and runs end to end: it draws through the
  modules, moves along its tracks, swaps, restores after a remount and shows its own status, label, gaze, theme and
  band. Tessa moved onto this path from the older drawing code; her public colour role names are kept
  (`mascot_colour_roles("tessa")`) and her restore button reads "Restore Tessa, <shown status>". A temporary bridge
  (`mascot-tessa-adapter.js`, switched on by `mascot.internal.useCharacterAdapter`) drew her through the modules in
  between; it and its tests went in #313, and `inst/characters/tessa.json` left the package.
* **Gaze.** Held look is `face.look_x` and `face.look_y` only. `compile()` records whether a face can look (a kit
  with an elliptical pupil); a faceless character or a kit of arcs, paths and dots has no gaze channels, and the
  host sends none.

<h3 id="dev-checks">Checks shared with R</h3>

* **Same counts as R (#304).** `mascot.runtime.bound()` counts all nine limits of the format for each band: parts and
  one accessory per slot, the face kit, kit effects (declared and started by a gesture), the ground shadow, mood and
  reduced-motion item changes, clips and gradients. Glow is counted on the box a shape covers after `ref` and
  `transform` moves, on the style a shared shape resolves to, and on the largest of an item's mood alternatives; R
  (`R/character-work.R`) got the last rule too. Scale ranges start from every part's resting scale; `null` keys of
  `set` tracks are ignored. A clip whose target is missing in a reachable variant throws `missing_reference` at
  `$.clip`. `check()` throws `budget` at `$` before painting. `lod.micro.glow: true` is refused with `budget` at `$`
  in both. Tests compare the browser with R at 1e-12 for the reference characters and Tessa in all three bands.
* **Band overrides (#303).** `lod.full` or any name other than `small` and `micro` is refused with `unknown_key`;
  so are an unknown key, a `face` flag other than `scale`, `lashes`, `brows` or `iris`, and a non-boolean `glow`.
* **Reserved capabilities (#306).** `extends`, `connector`, `ring_pulse`, `follow`, `particles`, `morph`, `blend`,
  `inputs`, `fit`, `wardrobe` and `vividness` are refused with code `capability` and "not supported by this version
  of mascot". A name in `requires` outside the eight supported capabilities is refused at `$.requires[n]`. A reserved
  name counts only as a key of a fixed-field object (as in `inst/format/character-v1.json`), so a colour role or a
  kit eye style called `follow` compiles. R reports the first problem in document order; the engine checks the
  top-level object first, so the two can differ when a reserved key comes before a structural error. Both results
  are pinned in `test-character-check.R` and `test-engine-parts-browser.R`.
* **Required gestures (#328).** A character needs a `wave` and a `nod` whose keyed values change. A wave needs a
  changing track on a non-root part; a nod can change any channel, `root` included.
* **Accessory ids (#312).** A worn accessory's parts are `wear__<accessory>__<part>`, and authored ids may not
  contain two underscores in a row (schema and browser check); `a_b`/`c` and `a`/`b_c` no longer collide.
  `mascot.parts.accessoryPartId()` builds the id in one place.
* **Format 1 for outside authors (#493).** `requires` is optional; a top-level `$schema`, `x_` keys and a `note` are
  accepted where R accepts them and never read (including in `mascot-motion.js`, `mascot-geometry.js` and a brand
  theme's `primary` and `secondary` slots). `mascot.parts.capabilities` lists supported and reserved names for the
  parity test. An unknown capability is named in the error; kit effect errors use the paths the R checker uses, such as
  `$.face.kit_definition.effects.<id>.items[<n>].clip`, and `fade_at` must be below 1.

<h3 id="dev-host">The host and Shiny</h3>

* **Life cycle.** `mascot-host.js` creates `window.mascot.host` (`mount`, `unmount`, `receive`, `state`), registers
  `MascotBinding` on `Shiny.inputBindings` and handles `mascot:update` messages. Updates that arrive before a mount
  wait in a queue limited to 20. Mount serials and per-field revision watermarks (`message.replay`, `message.fields`,
  `record.fields`) let the server replay state after a remount, and `playedGestures` stops a handled gesture from
  playing twice. `state()` reports `band`, `measures` and `offscreen`.
* **R-settled state (#305).** Shiny sends the latest complete accepted state for one mount generation. The host
  checks versioned envelopes, ignores stale revisions and ended generations, publishes mount and state snapshots with
  event priority and restores open bubbles with their remaining lifetime. A connection ledger keeps gesture use and
  bubble dismissal when an element is replaced. A duplicate live id leaves the first binding in charge. An unknown
  static UI token starts a one-time baseline exchange, so pages rendered before the server starts, and cached pages,
  bind after a restart; R checks the baseline fully before storing it. The canvas label follows the status of the
  character and mood shown.
* **New Shiny session (#426).** On `shiny:sessioninitialized` with a different session id, each live mascot resets
  its revision and its gesture and bubble watermarks and publishes its snapshot again as a `resume` start, keeping
  mount and generation. The page keeps what it shows until the new session sends a state, and a dismissed bubble
  does not reopen.
* **Connection loss (#70).** On `shiny:disconnected` every mascot switches to its worried mood and announces
  "Connection lost. Reload the page to continue." above the disconnect overlay (`mascot.css` raises it). Updates
  during the outage are kept and restored on `shiny:connected`.
* **Modules and re-rendering (#133, #273).** Examples cover nested modules, delayed `renderUI()` outputs and
  re-rendered containers. The host sends `input$<id>_minimised` (event priority) on minimise and restore.
* **Version (#464).** `mascot_dependency()` gives the `mascot.js` tag a `data-mascot-version` attribute, which
  `window.mascot.version` reads (`null` without it). A second copy of another version warns once through
  `console.warn` and the first stays.
* **Format-1 route.** `mascot.runtime.isFormat()` detects the description; `mascot.runtime.validate()` checks moods
  and gestures; `mascot.mount()` always uses `mascot.runtime`. A swap without a mood takes the incoming mood from the
  fallback chain. `mascot_preview()` resolves its theme the way `mascot()` does, so a character that is not built in
  passes the theme check there.
* **Comments.** Comments in the engine files say what the code does, without internal stage names or references to
  documents outside the package (#464).

<h3 id="dev-panels">Panels, clicks and menus</h3>

* **One panel system (#233, #237, #241, #244, #248, #249, #250, #254, #257, #263).** Speech bubbles, pop-up menus
  and action tooltips share `.mascot-panel`. `click` (`type: 'none' | 'action' | 'menu'`) replaced `popup_menu`. A
  clickable mascot is wrapped in one native `<button class="mascot-button">` that sends `input$<id>_click` (a
  monotonic counter that ignores key repeat and drag releases). `.mascot-tooltip` follows `WCAG` 1.4.13: a 150 ms
  pointer-leave grace and a shared `Escape` listener.
* **Placement of panels.** `inkBox()` scans the alpha channel for the drawn box when a menu or tooltip opens;
  `placePanel()` chooses the side (`auto`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, falling back to the opposite side or `auto`)
  inside `clipBounds()` and positions `--_mascot-panel-tail`. Only one menu is open at a time (`openMenus`); bubble
  timers pause while a menu is open or the mascot is minimised, and focus moves before controls are hidden. Panels
  fade out over 150 ms, using an inert DOM clone.
* **Gaze.** `gazeSide()`, `gazePose()` and `refreshGaze()` hold `look` and `lookY` towards the open menu's resolved
  `data-side` or the active bubble, allowing for horizontal `flip`.
* **Menus (#349, #350).** Only action buttons send `input$<id>_click`; opening or closing a menu leaves the count
  alone, and choosing an item sends `input$<id>_menu` with event priority. A menu click setting carries a `disabled`
  flag: the button stays focusable (`aria-disabled`) but opens nothing and sends nothing; disabling an open menu
  closes it.
* **Clicks through the bubble space (#506).** `.mascot-bubble-region` has `pointer-events: none` and `.mascot-bubble`
  restores `auto` for itself and its contents, so clicks reach page controls around a bubble.
* **Inline bubbles.** While one shows, the host also watches sibling layout changes so the message stays inside the
  viewport.

<h3 id="dev-placement">Placement, dragging and minimising</h3>

* **Floating placement.** `portal()` moves a floating mascot to `document.body` and leaves a `.mascot-source`
  placeholder span, so the `unbindAll` call of Shiny and the source container's visibility and styles still work. A
  `ResizeObserver` scales the canvas by the device pixel ratio, and the offset of `#shiny-notification-panel` is
  tracked.
* **Phone sizing (#259, #261, #264, #266).** With `small_screen: "auto"` (`validateSize()`), floating mascots cap their
  default size at 96 pixels at `<= 575.98px`
  (`.mascot[data-floating="true"][data-small-screen="auto"]`).
* **Dragging (#220, #222, #225, #229, #231, #232).** Pointer capture, `listenDrag()`, `drop()`, `cancelDrag()`,
  `clampPoint()` and `nearestCorner()`, a 4-pixel threshold (`dragThreshold`), click suppression after a drag in the
  capture phase, a 200 ms snap animation and `input$<id>_position`. `snap` goes to the nearest corner and `free`
  stays where it is dropped. The minimised restore button drags too.
* **Snap corner (#513).** `drop()` picks the corner with `nearestCorner()` from the drop point, with the mascot's own
  size, before `clampPoint()`; a mascot taller or wider than the window less its margins used to be clamped first and
  snapped back to the bottom or right.
* **Minimise and restore (#275, #276).** Minimising and restoring animate with Web Animations (240 ms transform and
  opacity, using a `.mascot-motion-copy` canvas clone). The host re-measures and calls `controller.redraw()` when
  restoring, when the animation finishes or is cancelled, and whenever `measure()` changes the canvas size, so the
  mascot is sharp at full device resolution. `redraw()` repeats `drawFrame()` without moving time or the activity
  window.

<h3 id="dev-motion">Motion</h3>

* **Tracks (#299).** `mascot.motion.tracks`: `normalise()` and `sample()` for `[[at, value, ease?], ...]` and
  `{ mode, keys }` tracks (add and set modes, `null` as the mood base, discrete values that switch at keys, the
  easing curves `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out`, `ease_in_out` and `step`, exact rest at the end); `compile()` for needs and
  fallback traversal (missing, cyclic and unplayable chains fail with `{ code, path }`), target-part checks and the
  1 to 150 frame budget; `settings()`; `fit()` for late effects; `frameAt()` for interruption, reduction, a
  five-second absolute deadline, multiplicative breathing, blink skipping and separate effect instances; `drawn()`.
  Unknown gesture, channel, easing and effect names are errors; morph, blend and particles stay reserved. The idle
  `extra` start time comes from `state.extraAt` (the host's seeded value; `null` suppresses it).
* **Swapping characters (#307).** The outgoing character waves (its `wave` tracks over the captured channels) and fades
  over thirty frames, the incoming one waves and fades in over thirty, composited once through a private canvas, with
  durations fitted to the incoming activity window. A new target mid-fade keeps the exit time that remains; asking for
  the exiting character again reverses; a mood change mid-swap commits without a wiggle; a gesture during a swap is
  dropped; reduced motion or `swap: false` is instant.
* **Separate switches (#239, #267).** `animate` became independent switches for `idle`, `mood_change`, `gestures`,
  `swap`, `minimising`, `restoring`, `others` and per-panel `messages` (`bubble`, `tooltip`, `menu`);
  `mascot.motion.settings` and `mascot.motion.panels` are frozen exports. In development mode a
  `shiny:client-message` warns when a server gesture is skipped because `gestures = false`.

<h3 id="dev-styling">Styling and theming</h3>

* **Public hooks (#260, #270).** `--mascot-panel-*`, `--mascot-restore-*` and `--mascot-z-index` are public; layout
  variables are private `--_mascot-*` (`size`, `source-*`, `drag-*`, `menu-*`, `tooltip-*`, `panel-tail`,
  `notification-offset`), so user style sheets win over Bootstrap and page defaults. For a floating mascot moved to
  `document.body`, the inherited public hooks are copied from the source anchor to `--_mascot-source-*`.
* **Bubble space class (#558).** `.mascot-bubble-region` is a public class next to `.mascot-bubble`; hide it with
  `display: none` on a page that never shows a bubble. Renaming it needs a deprecation. `?mascot_styling` lists it
  and a test checks that `mascot()` puts it on the page.
* **Page themes.** `resolveTheme()`, `shadeColour()` (`HSL` lightness and saturation shifts from the leader roles in
  `description.follows`), `colourContrast()` (`WCAG` relative luminance, 3:1 warnings) and `pageMode()`, which watches
  `[data-bs-theme]` and `body.quarto-dark` / `quarto-light` and defaults to light.
* **Palettes (#336, #358).** R resolves a named palette; the host receives its id and light and dark leader colours
  apart from explicit overrides and applies palette colours, then role overrides, then CSS. R decides whether a
  palette is kept on a character swap and warns when the incoming character lacks the id. Outside Shiny, a host patch
  resolves a shared palette against the incoming character or drops it. When the incoming character's own colours
  carry the palette id (`native_palette`), the id is kept and no palette colours are applied, as for `original`.

<h3 id="dev-performance">Performance</h3>

* **Page changes and layout (#295).** `relevantMutation()` filters `MutationObserver` records, so changes outside a
  mascot's ancestor chain, its `.mascot-source` anchor, `<head>` styles or `#shiny-notification-panel` do no work.
  Page refreshes and theme-mode changes coalesce through `schedulePageRefresh()` into one `requestAnimationFrame`
  per burst; changes confined to private host style properties are ignored.
* **Off-screen mascots (#295).** A shared, reference-counted `IntersectionObserver` (`watchViewport()`) calls
  `controller.holdVisibility()` when a mascot leaves or re-enters the viewport. The hold is independent of user pause
  and activity: returning does not draw, renew the five-second window or override another pause, and a moving
  player continues from its saved frame. The observer disconnects with the last unmount.
* **Character data once per page (#497).** `mascot()` puts a built-in character's
  `<script type="application/json" data-mascot-character="<id>">` block in the page head through an HTML dependency
  named `mascot-character-<id>`; a custom character's block stays inside its element. `characterScript(id, scope)`
  in `mascot.js` finds it: the element's own block, then one outside every mascot element, never another mascot's.
  `readCharacter(id, scope)` parses it, and the host's `template-needed` recovery reads through `characterScript()`.
* **Caches.** `bound()` is frozen and cached per character and band; a band that passed once is not checked again.
  The channel table of a plain frame is one object per player.

<h3 id="dev-removed">What was removed</h3>

* **The older drawing path (#463).** `mascot-draw.js` is gone and `mascot_dependency()` no longer lists it: about
  2,090 lines and 87 KB less JavaScript on every page. `mascot.js` keeps `fps`, `readCharacter()` and `validColour()`
  (its load-twice guard keys on `readCharacter`); `draw()`, `validateCharacter()` and `checkCharacter()` are removed.
  `mascot-motion.js` keeps `tracks`, `shared` (with `swapTiming`), `settings` and `panels`; its older player,
  `pose()`, `frame()` and `validate()` are removed. `update({ character })` with a description that is not format
  version 1 fails with "update.character: expected a character with format_version 1".
* **The Tessa bridge (#313).** See the Tessa item under drawing. `mascot.geometry.bandBound()` and `checkBudget()`
  went with it; `checkWork()` stays.
* **Namespace hint (#392).** `suggestNamespace()`, a two-second development-mode hint for a missing `ns()`, could not
  be reached from Shiny, because R drops an update for an id that is not mounted. The module rule stays in
  `?mascot` and `?update_mascot`.
* **`simplify_when_small` (#219, #221).** The separate small-size face drawing is gone; detail bands replace it.

</details>

# mascot 0.0.2

## 2026-10-06 — Animated character swaps (`ea35c6f`, #147, #173)

**In brief:** Swapping from one character to another waves and fades the old character out over one second,
then fades the new character in while waving over one second, handling rapid mid-swap changes and reversals
smoothly.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: added `mascot.motion.frame` (`sceneFrame(ch, state, n)`) and `SwapState`
  (`at`, `until`, `outFrames`, `inFrames`, `opacity`, `outgoing` snapshot with `wave` and `recovery`
  continuations), off-screen buffer blending (`layer` canvas in `drawFrame()`) so part-level alpha never
  leaks during fade-out and fade-in, `controller.current()`, and `options.onChange(snapshot)`.
* `inst/www/mascot.js`: added `validColour` and cached character validation in a `WeakMap`.

## 2026-10-06 — Frame-stepping motion engine and five-second player (`853b448`, #27, #145)

**In brief:** Added `mascot-motion.js` for mood transitions (wiggle or hop), deterministic seeded blinking
and breathing, one-off `nod` and `wave` gestures, `prefers-reduced-motion` support, and a canvas player
that automatically stops its `requestAnimationFrame` loop after five seconds (150 frames).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: added `window.mascot.motion` (`{ pose, validate }`) and
  `window.mascot.mount(canvas, ch, options)` returning
  `{ seek, update, setMood, gesture, pause, play, destroy }`; implemented `LCG` hash blinking
  (`Math.imul((seed >>> 0) ^ i, 1664525) + 1013904223`), smooth breathing fade over the final third of the
  150-frame window, and atomic `preparePatch()` validation.

## 2026-10-03 — Data-driven character engine (`4ba964a`, `f642d19`, #52, #66, #137, #138)

**In brief:** Turned Tessa's hard-coded drawing code into a generic engine (`mascot.js` and
`mascot-draw.js`) that validates and draws any character from its `JSON` description
(`inst/characters/<id>.json`).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot.js`: added data-driven `readCharacter`, `validateCharacter` and `draw` under
  `window.mascot` (`fps = 30`). Colour validation and `WeakMap` validation caching follow in `ea35c6f`.
* `inst/www/mascot-draw.js`: added `window.mascot.drawing` (`svgPath` parser for absolute `M/L/Q/C/Z`
  commands, `hexPath`, `drawPart`, `resolvePose`, `guardPose`, `anchors` returning world coordinates and
  2x2 linear matrices, `accessories` slot validation, and `FACE_STYLE` overrides).
